record.paper_title: Twenty Open Questions in Supersymmetric Particle Physics
record.original_question: Supergravity predicts a gravitino whose mass and interactions are set by the supersymmetry-breaking scale, and gravitinos can be thermally produced in the early universe or produced by decays of MSSM superpartners. Are gravitinos cosmologically dangerous relics, and what ranges of gravitino mass, reheating temperature, dilution by late inflation, and baryogenesis mechanism avoid overclosure, excess relativistic species, supernova bounds, or late nucleosynthesis-damaging decays?

evidence.quote: Question #11 Are gravitinos dangerous to cosmology?
In the early universe, gravitinos are believed to have existed in thermal equilibrium with a plasma of hidden- and visible-sector fields.
Calculating the relevant cross-sections and solving the Boltzmann equation allows one to put an upper bound on the mass of a stable gravitino in order to avoid overclosing the universe.
For the first two cases, a period of late inflation... can dilute away the gravitino problem. However, any baryon densities present before this late inflation would also be diluted away.

artifact.status_search_result: The gravitino problem remains an active area of research with no definitive resolution. Recent work (2024–2025), including full one-loop calculations of thermal gravitino production beyond the hard thermal loop approximation, continues to refine upper bounds on the reheating temperature (typically 10^7–10^10 GeV depending on gravitino mass and scenario). The viability of various baryogenesis mechanisms in conjunction with these constraints is still being analyzed, and no single scenario has been singled out as the established cosmological history. The question is therefore considered open, though substantial partial constraints exist.

status_evidence.title: Gravitino Thermal Production, Dark Matter, and Reheating of the Universe
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) full one-loop calculation of gravitino thermal production rate providing updated constraints on reheating temperature in gravitino dark matter scenarios.
status_evidence.claim: Active research in 2024 continues to update constraints on T_R from gravitino production, indicating the problem is not closed.

status_evidence.title: Big-bang nucleosynthesis with unstable gravitino and upper bound on the reheating temperature
status_evidence.snippet: BBN with unstable gravitinos yields scenario-dependent upper bounds on T_R.
status_evidence.claim: BBN constraints give upper bounds on T_R that depend on gravitino mass and decay properties, with no single resolution.

status_evidence.title: Constraints on the reheating temperature in gravitino dark matter scenarios
status_evidence.snippet: Constraints on T_R in gravitino dark matter scenarios remain model-dependent.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple viable regions of parameter space remain, indicating the problem is open.
